title: Existence of a zeta assignment dominating the group averages in the extended formulation of symmetric Benders cuts
author: Christopher Hojny, C\'edric Roy, Anonymous (e-print placeholder line)
work: A Framework for Handling and Exploiting Symmetry in Benders Decomposition
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Lemma 12 (source label 'rmk:zeta-lb'): for every x in [0,1]^n there is a vector zeta in [0,1]^n satisfying the two constraint families (9) and (10) of the extended formulation of symmetric Benders cuts, with the additional domination property that each entry zeta^k_G is bounded by the average x(G)/|G| of its group. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a genuine construction rather than an algebraic identity: the authors first compute the exact interval in which a feasible entry must lie, then show that this interval is non-empty for every k, then build the candidate entry from the tight lower end of that interval and prove that the resulting sequence is non-increasing in k, and finally repair the possibility that the candidate is negative by taking its maximum with zero, verifying that the repaired vector still satisfies both constraint families and the domination bound. That construction is the technical heart of the paper's proof that the extended formulation has a strictly weaker LP relaxation than the cut pool model, and it is not reachable by routine textbook manipulation. The retained uncounted context carries the whole extended-formulation passage, so the counted proof is delivered with the definitions of the zeta-variables, of the generic extended-formulation cut, of Theorem 9 and of the restated Proposition 11 that it serves.
